goal: Add a Task Managers section (Basecamp first) to the harness: an offline-tested reader CLI with login and refresh, an owner-gated dashboard section, bounded untrusted seed packets kept out of the audit database, dashboard-started delegated runs that end in a draft pull request, and owner-gated write-back.
constraints: Python standard library only; no new Rust crates.
Reader commands send GET only; comment and complete are the only Basecamp writes, each behind an explicit owner-gated POST.
Secrets and tokens are never printed, logged or placed in argv.
Every Task Managers dashboard route is gated with OwnerCheck; POSTs also need CSRF.
Delegated runs stop at a draft pull request; nothing merges.
Tests run offline against a fake Basecamp server.
Leave the other session's uncommitted hunks in ui.rs, workflow.rs, styles.css and turn-context.html intact.

non_goals.description: No changes to the guard, denylist or hook settings (human-only files).
No providers other than Basecamp; the others are listed as not connected.
No dashboard login route; login stays a CLI command.
Prototype files and real Basecamp data stay out of the commit.

acceptance.criterion: Reader, cache and CLI pass against the fake server, GET only, no secret output
Login exchange and refresh rotate the token file atomically at 0600
Seed bounds hold on the injection fixture and the draft contract validates
Fenced task-manager text is withheld from prompt and context events
Run state machine reaches a draft PR through both approval gates and never merges
Comment and complete each send exactly one POST; readers send none
Dashboard routes are owner-gated, CSRF-checked and render with the feature off
The audit service on this machine serves /tasks with live Basecamp data to the owner
